findings.quote: Once both torches are visible, the outlets are to be opened immediately.
findings.problem: Greek: γενομένων δὲ φανερῶν ἀμφοτέρων ἅμα τῶν πυρσῶν καθελεῖν. εἶτ᾽ εὐθέως ἀφεῖναι τοὺς αὐλίσκους ῥεῖν. The lowering of the torches (καθελεῖν) is a separate step before the outlets are opened; the English omits it.
findings.proposed_fix: Once both torches are visible at the same time, they are to be lowered, and then the outlets are to be opened at once.

findings.quote: And that is why properly organized history is supremely useful in this matter too.
findings.problem: Greek: διὸ καὶ τοῦτο γίνεται τῆς δεόντως ἱστορίας συντεταγμένης ὠφελιμώτατον. The subject is τοῦτο (this very part/digression), which becomes the most useful element of a duly composed history (partitive genitive); the English makes history itself the subject and loses the superlative's partitive sense.
findings.proposed_fix: And that is why this too proves the most useful part of a properly composed history.

units.note: Also: ἑπτὰ καὶ πέντε στίχους is literally 'seven and five lines'; English 'five or seven' is a defensible idiomatic reading, not flagged.

findings.quote: In this engagement the king’s horse was killed after being wounded,
findings.problem: Greek has two lacunae: τὸν μὲν ἵππον συμβαίνει *** ἀποθανεῖν τραυματισθέντα ***. The English reads on as if the text were whole.
findings.proposed_fix: In this engagement it happened that the horse [text missing] was killed, having been wounded [text missing],

units.note: Text is gapped in the Greek; do not supply the missing words.
